title: Fully Fluctuating Sleepy Consensus from Minimal Assumptions
abstract: Bitcoin's proof-of-work (PoW)-based protocol is remarkable for how little it asks of its participants. Not only can miners take breaks from work whenever they please, but it is almost unique in offering a path of contrition: corrupt miners can reclaim honest status simply by resuming mining on the longest chain. The protocol only requires that honest miners hold the majority of computational power at any given time. Analogous proof-of-stake (PoS) protocols, usually formalized via the sleepy model of Pass and Shi (2017), have fallen short of matching this robustness. In fact, sleepy consensus protocols in the plain PKI model must heavily restrict fluctuations in adversarial participation over time. The recent work of Efron, Neu, and Pitassi (2025) enables fully fluctuating participation in the sleepy model by introducing the external adversary model. Their protocol, however, relies on verifiable delay functions (VDFs), a strong cryptographic primitive that somewhat resembles PoW, by assuming that the adversary cannot compute sequential work significantly faster than honest nodes. In this work, we design a sleepy consensus protocol for fully fluctuating participation with an external adversary under an honest majority, from minimal assumptions: a public key infrastructure (PKI) and a verifiable random function (VRF). In particular, we make no VDF or hardware assumptions. Our key technique is graded wakeness, a novel primitive that allows nodes to form consistent opinions on which other nodes are awake. We further extend our protocol to handle uncorruption, where corrupt nodes return to honesty. This extension requires only a mild additional assumption on the unpredictability of VRF outputs for liveness.

title: MuyBridge: Mobile Human Center-of-Mass Estimation from Monocular Video via Sparse Fusion
abstract: The 3D center of mass (CoM) is a primary quantity in the biomechanical analysis of sport, rehabilitation, and clinical movement, yet existing 3D pose tracking, mesh recovery, and multi-view triangulation methods either optimize 3D keypoint accuracy without anatomical constraints or carry compute and capture infrastructure too heavy to deploy where CoM tracking is most useful. As a result, the metric CoM remains difficult for coaches and movement analysts to measure from a single camera where athletes train and compete. In this work, we introduce MuyBridge, an on-device system that estimates the athlete's segmental center of mass trajectory from a single phone camera video stream. MuyBridge couples a compact 2D pose network and a distilled single-step monocular depth network through an analytic metric fusion that uses anatomical and physical priors to anchor the metric CoM, requiring no 3D or task-specific supervision. Evaluated on the athletic movements of AthletePose3D (running, track and field, and figure skating), MuyBridge achieves 33-41 mm vertical CoM error and 2.3-6.6% absolute-relative range error (AbsRel) under a one-time calibration, and produces CoM estimates at the 63 FPS pose-estimation rate using asynchronous 2.86 Hz depth updates on iPhone 15. Code is available at: https://github.com/Abradshaw1/Muybridge

title: An Infinite Family of Non-Rational VOAs from Strongly Coupled 4d Higgsless SCFTs
abstract: We study an infinite family of strongly coupled four-dimensional mathcal N=2 superconformal field theories (SCFTs) distinguished by a trivial Higgs branch, known as the (A_2,D_{3m+1}) Argyre-Douglas theories. We propose that their associated vertex operator algebras (VOAs) are the doublet algebras mathcal A(4m+2), an infinite family of non-rational vertex operator superalgebras with a remarkably simple strong generating set of only three fields. We provide several highly nontrivial checks of this proposal. In particular, we reproduce the four-dimensional conformal anomalies a and c from the VOA and analytically prove the exact equality between the Schur index of the SCFT and the supercharacter of the VOA. A key ingredient is a diagonal-gauging realization of the (A_2,D_{3m+1}) theories in terms of two simpler building blocks, which makes the Schur-index computation tractable. Remarkably, we find that the resulting Schur index of the (A_2,D_{3m+1}) theory coincides with that of mathcal N=4 SU(2) Super-Yang-Mills theory, up to an overall prefactor and an appropriate identification of fugacities. We also discuss a generalization to the two-parameter family (A_{2s},D_{(2s+1)m+1}), whose members likewise have trivial Higgs branches and admit diagonal-gauging realizations. A particularly interesting subfamily is (A_{2s},D_{2s+2}), for which the four-dimensional conformal anomalies coincide, a=c. Our results reveal a systematic connection between Higgsless SCFTs, diagonal gauging, and strongly finite but non-rational vertex operator algebras.

title: VoRTeC: Taming Foundation Flow for One-step Real time Video Compression
abstract: Ultra-low bitrate video compression still faces critical challenges: traditional neural video compression inevitably introduces blurring artifacts, while diffusion-based generative video compression suffers from excessive decoding latency and poor temporal consistency. To address these issues, we propose $\mathtt{VoRTeC}$, a Video Compression framework built upon a foundational flow model (Wan2.1). By compactly encoding latent video representations, predicting the positions of compressed representations along flow trajectories, and integrating multi-scale priors, $\mathtt{VoRTeC}$ enables the compressor to harness generative video flow priors effectively. Without accessing the parameters or gradients of flow matching networks, our framework achieves one-step decoding and reconstructions with high perceptual fidelity. Meanwhile, we maintain consistency across frame groups via tail-frame reuse and prior caching. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method reduces bit consumption by 58\% compared to prior diffusion-based approaches, with decoding speed boosted by 3 to 197 times: $\mathtt{VoRTeC}$ achieves a decoding speed of 13 FPS at 720p and 32 FPS at 480p.

title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A State of the Art Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Notarization analysis of a minimal Mach-O binary
abstract: This article is meant to show a solid reverse engineering methodology, and how we work with notarization. We decided to use a very simple program (only four bytes of code) rather than something more complex exactly to highlight the undertaken steps. We opted for this solution also to avoid copyright breaches. This exercise will show that only four bytes of code end up in a 16888-byte program, due to the dynamic linking and other mechanisms that are out of the current scope; three out of five pages are zeros, and the signature covers those too. Interestingly, Apple notarizes a program containing just four bytes of executable code. This has been properly shown; however stapling fails with error 73: the stapler looks for Contents/CodeResources inside a file that it had just identified as not being a directory. The ticket is generated and downloaded regardless: 45 bytes of content, 20 of which make up the cdhash, containing the CloudKit record timestamp. Even without the ticket, the binary is recognised as notarized; verification takes place online.Every byte of the binary pertaining to the signature is accounted for, including the blob. No Mach-O header or other similar analyses have been performed, for clarity and brevity purposes.

title: 基于量子拓扑的自适应算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive algorithm based on quantum topology, designed to optimize complex systems and achieve high-precision calculations. Traditional algorithms rely on classical computation, while this approach leverages the unique properties of quantum topology to offer enhanced precision and adaptability. We present a conceptual framework for this algorithm, detailing the core mechanism, justification for its novelty, and potential applications in diverse fields. The paper explores the advantages of quantum topology in parameter optimization and demonstrates the algorithm's effectiveness through mathematical analysis and illustrative examples. The focus is on the algorithmic design, theoretical justification, and preliminary results, with a limited focus on experimental validation.

title: 自适应拓扑几何的动态构建
abstract: This paper explores the potential of self-adaptive topology geometry, utilizing quantum entanglement to generate complex and scalable topological structures. Traditional approaches often struggle with intricate geometries, necessitating computationally intensive methods. We propose a novel algorithm that leverages quantum entanglement to dynamically reshape geometry, allowing for the creation of structures beyond the limitations of classical computation. This work introduces a "quantum topological deformation" mechanism, enabling instantaneous transformations and localized structural evolution through entangled states. The core claim is that this approach offers a fundamentally new pathway for topology generation, surpassing the capabilities of existing algorithms. This study investigates the algorithm's capabilities and potential applications, focusing on its ability to produce topologically rich and scalable structures.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding with Topological Error Correction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum information encoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement coupled with topological error correction codes. The core claim is to design a robust encoding scheme that utilizes entanglement to generate quantum states and topological error correction to mitigate the effects of noise during transmission, ultimately achieving high fault-tolerance and efficient quantum information transfer. The proposed mechanism constructs a quantum entanglement network by combining the error correction information from a specific topological code, such as a lattice code, with the quantum entanglement state. Nodes in the network control the encoding and decoding of this error correction information, effectively correcting errors introduced by environmental noise while preserving the integrity of the entangled state. This approach addresses a key limitation of traditional entanglement-based encoding schemes, which often lack the inherent redundancy offered by topological structures, thereby significantly enhancing the reliability of quantum information transmission. The theoretical framework and key concepts are presented within this document.

title: Probability Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic adaptive neural network (PANN) architecture designed to enhance model generalization and adaptability. Traditional neural networks often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively learn from diverse data. Our proposed PANN employs a probabilistic distribution to dynamically adjust network parameters, allowing the network to adapt to the underlying data distribution during training. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments involving complex datasets, showcasing significant improvements in performance metrics such as accuracy, robustness, and generalization. The core of the algorithm lies in the probabilistic parameter update mechanism, which leverages the data distribution to guide the learning process. This leads to a more robust and adaptable model capable of handling variations in input data. We present the results of our experiments, highlighting the advantages of this approach compared to existing techniques.

title: 基于自适应量子路径的量子算法优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum path algorithms to improve the efficiency and accuracy of quantum algorithms. Traditional quantum algorithm optimization often relies on static, pre-defined quantum paths, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts quantum paths based on the system's state, offering a more flexible and robust approach. The core mechanism involves a quantum path evolution algorithm that continuously refines the quantum state to achieve optimal results. This adaptive nature allows for improved performance in complex scenarios compared to static optimization techniques. We analyze the performance of this framework through a series of simulations, demonstrating a significant improvement in algorithm execution time and error correction capabilities. The results highlight the potential of adaptive quantum path algorithms to revolutionize quantum algorithm design and optimization.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Compression in Symbolic Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for compression of symbolic computation outputs, focusing on the limitations of current approaches and proposing a novel methodology grounded in information theory. Traditional compression techniques applied to symbolic expressions often fall short of optimal performance due to a failure to recognize and exploit the inherent redundancy within these representations. This work establishes a core claim: existing algorithms do not fully leverage the redundancy present in symbolic computations. We introduce a mechanism utilizing information-theoretic measures, specifically entropy, to precisely quantify the compressibility of symbolic expressions. The development of compression algorithms is then driven by these entropy distributions, moving beyond the constraints of methods like Huffman coding. Through this approach, we aim to define information-theoretic limits for symbolic compression, offering a rigorous framework for future research and algorithm design. The key contribution lies in shifting the focus from heuristic optimization to a theoretically sound foundation, providing a pathway to significantly improved compression rates for symbolic computation systems.

title: Multi-Dimensional Spatial Information Retrieval via Quantum Algorithms: Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm for optimizing multi-dimensional spatial information retrieval. Traditional information retrieval methods struggle with the exponential growth of complexity in high-dimensional spaces. We propose a quantum approach leveraging superposition and interference to drastically improve search efficiency. The core concept involves mapping the retrieval space into a quantum state space, utilizing quantum entanglement for parallel search across multiple dimensions, and employing quantum measurement to rapidly pinpoint the target information. The algorithm's performance is theoretically analyzed, demonstrating a potential speedup compared to classical algorithms. Specifically, we outline a framework for constructing a quantum index and detailing the steps involved in the search process. The key elements of the algorithm are the quantum state preparation, entanglement generation, and the final measurement stage. We provide a mathematical formulation of the core operations, focusing on the quantum circuit design and the probability amplitudes involved. The optimization strategy relies on minimizing the number of quantum gates required while maintaining the algorithm's effectiveness. The ultimate goal is to provide a robust and scalable quantum solution for spatial information retrieval, addressing the limitations of current classical methods.

title: 基于动态图的知识发现系统
abstract: This paper proposes a Dynamic Graph-Based Knowledge Discovery System (DGBKDS) designed to facilitate real-time knowledge discovery and updates. The core premise lies in leveraging the dynamic graph data structure to represent and analyze evolving knowledge. The system utilizes graph algorithms for knowledge graph analysis and mining, combined with machine learning techniques to optimize the knowledge discovery process. Unlike traditional approaches that often rely on static knowledge graphs, DGBKDS addresses the challenge of incorporating temporal information and adapting to changing relationships. The system's architecture incorporates mechanisms for tracking entity and relationship changes, enabling continuous knowledge evolution. The primary contribution lies in the methodology for constructing a dynamic knowledge graph and applying algorithms specifically designed for temporal graph analysis, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency in knowledge discovery compared to static graph representations. The system's potential impact extends across diverse domains where knowledge is inherently dynamic, such as social network analysis, fraud detection, and scientific discovery.

title: Neural Symbolic Dynamic Planning
abstract: This paper introduces Neural Symbolic Dynamic Planning (NSDP), a novel framework that integrates the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning to address complex decision-making problems. Traditional reinforcement learning often struggles with local optima and requires extensive exploration. NSDP overcomes these limitations by combining a neural network for state representation and reward prediction with a rule-based symbolic reasoning engine for action planning. The core mechanism leverages dynamic programming, allowing the neural network and symbolic engine to iteratively refine the decision-making process. We posit that this synergistic approach enables more efficient learning and optimization of complex strategies, surpassing the capabilities of conventional reinforcement learning methods. This work outlines the architecture, the dynamic programming algorithm used for interaction, and presents a theoretical justification for its efficacy. We demonstrate the potential of NSDP to tackle challenging problems requiring both perceptual understanding and logical deduction. ---

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Cooperative Evolvability
abstract: Traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods often face challenges in achieving robust, long-term cooperation, particularly within dynamic and evolving environments. This paper introduces a novel framework, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Cooperative Evolvability (MARE), designed to address these limitations. The core of MARE lies in an "evolvability" mechanism, which empowers agents to dynamically adjust their internal reward functions and learning strategies based on the observed behavior of their peers. This dynamic adaptation facilitates cooperative learning and allows agents to effectively respond to and adapt to complex, changing environments. We formally define the MARE framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. We present a mathematical formulation of the core principles, highlighting the convergence properties and adaptive capabilities of the system. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement in MARL, demonstrating improved cooperation and adaptability compared to conventional methods. The theoretical analysis and conceptual design aim to provide a foundation for future research and development in this area.

title: 基于拓扑结构的自适应量子纠错
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental principle in quantum mechanics, offering unparalleled capabilities for secure communication and computation. However, maintaining the coherence of quantum states is a significant challenge, particularly in the presence of environmental noise. This paper introduces a novel quantum error correction scheme based on topological structures, aiming to enhance the robustness and fidelity of quantum systems. We propose a self-adaptive algorithm that dynamically adjusts the quantum state to mitigate errors, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement. The core mechanism revolves around exploiting the dynamic evolution of the quantum state to suppress errors, ultimately improving the overall reliability of quantum information processing. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in mitigating specific error sources. The proposed method offers a promising avenue for advancing the practical implementation of quantum technologies.

title: Integration of Large Language Models in Layered Software Systems: A Clean Architecture and CQRS Case Study
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly incorporated into software systems. Their non-deterministic behavior, external hosting, response latency, and operational cost create challenges for established design approaches such as Clean Architecture. This paper examines the integration of an LLM component into a layered software system and compares three possible placements within Clean Architecture: Domain, Application, and Infrastructure. The evaluation considers dependency management, testability, separation of concerns, and implementation complexity. The study proposes an approach in which the LLM is implemented in the Infrastructure layer and accessed through an interface defined in the Application layer. This approach is combined with the Command and Query Responsibility Segregation pattern to isolate LLM interaction within dedicated query handlers. The proposed pattern is demonstrated through the implementation of Budget, a personal finance tracking system that uses GPT-4.1 to convert free-form natural language input into structured transaction records. The results show that placement in the infrastructure layer provides the clearest separation between business logic and external AI services and avoids the introduction of non-deterministic behavior into the core application logic.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Granular Avalanche Dynamics on Curved Topography
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free framework for solving governing equations, but their application to granular avalanche dynamics over curved terrain remains largely unexplored. This study extends a depth-averaged PINN formulation based on the Savage-Hutter equations to an exponentially curved chute with spatially varying inclination and a strain-rate-dependent Mohr-Coulomb earth-pressure closure. The model is validated against measured front- and rear-edge trajectories from a laboratory granular-avalanche experiment, with selected observations withheld from training. A staged temporal curriculum proved essential for accurate prediction, reducing the held-out trajectory error by approximately two orders of magnitude compared with training over the full time domain from the outset. Sparse-data experiments further showed that observation placement was more influential than observation number within the configurations tested. Four observations bracketing the transition from acceleration to deceleration achieved nearly the same accuracy as the eight-observation reference configuration, whereas observations clustered at early or late times performed poorly. The results demonstrate the importance of both training strategy and informative data placement when applying PINNs to granular flows over curved topography.

title: Quantum low-density lattice codes
abstract: Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes provide a family of promising schemes for encoding discrete quantum information (qudits) into infinite-dimensional bosonic modes based on mathematical lattices. While such codes, when concatenated with discrete-variable codes, are relatively well studied, the construction and decoding of native GKP codes has largely remained open due to the computationally hard problems encountered. To address this challenge, we advocate a strategy of co-designing the decoder and the quantum error-correcting code itself by constructing lattices for which decoding is feasible: The requirement of efficient decoding effectively determines the quantum error-correcting code. This construction is built on classical low-density lattice codes (LDLCs), a lattice analogue of low-density parity-check codes, here lifted to families of GKP codes. Concretely, we introduce quantum versions of classical, randomly constructed LDLCs. We show that after suitable dimensionality reduction these codes have code properties comparable to or better than concatenated GKP-surface codes of equal number of modes. However, the GKP-LDLCs constructed here do not have a strictly sparse parity check matrix, which motivates our study of the performance of natively analog message-passing decoders originally developed for LDLCs when applied to concatenated GKP-LDPC codes. We show that the fully analog, linear-time decoder achieves performances close to state-of-the-art hybrid qubit-analog decoders. To facilitate future research on the structure and performance of general GKP codes, the relevant source code will be released in open-source Julia packages LatticeDecoder.jl and SymplecticGKP.jl.

title: A Two-Variable Zeta Function for a Parity-Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: The Exceptional t = -1 Slice and Gaussian Boundary Layers
abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter Q-recursion $ widetilde Q(1)=widetilde Q(2)=1,qquad widetilde Q(n)=widetilde Q(n-widetilde Q(n-1)) +widetilde Q(n-widetilde Q(n-2))+(-1)^n, and the associated two-variable Dirichlet series Z_{widetilde Q}(s,t)=sum_{nge1}n^{-s}widetilde Q(n)^{-t}. The estimate \widetilde Q(n)=n/2+O(n/\log n) gives the exact domain of absolute convergence Re(s+t)>1. With w=s+t, we separate the universal term 2^tζ(w) and derive exact transport, frequency-position, and dyadic renormalization identities. The main result concerns t=-1. For E(n)=2\widetilde Q(n)-n and A(X)=\sum_{n\le X}E(n), the binary-arch clock yields A(X)=Xlog_2X+XΩ!left(log_23X{32}right) +O!left(X{log X}right), where Ω is an explicit continuous periodic function. This continues the normalized correction to Rew>0 and yields a boundary resonance lattice: a double resonance at w=0 and simple resonances at 2πi m/\log2. After subtracting the full-slice order-X skeleton, we analyze the negative-even arch channel. Its companion-forest layers have a weak Gaussian limit, and a canonical subsequence realizes the optimal n/\log n pointwise scale with an explicit signed constant. The negative-arch mass satisfies A_r=512{92π}16^r{sqrt r} left(1-13{16r}+O(r^{-2})right). We do not claim a full-slice continuation across Rew=0$.

title: Compositional Spectral Prompts for LLM-based Online Time Series Forecasting
abstract: To address the sequential and evolving nature of time series, the Online Time Series Forecasting (OTSF) task has been extensively studied in multiple domains. Existing research focuses on adapting to non-stationary environments by employing memory buffer-based retrieval strategies. However, we observe that such frameworks struggle with long-term adaptation and fail to generalize to unseen patterns. To this end, we introduce CoSPOT, an LLM-based online time series forecasting framework that leverages a pre-trained LLM as the backbone online forecaster, motivated by its strong few-shot capabilities. For efficient online adaptation, CoSPOT keeps the LLM frozen and employs compositional spectral prompts grounded in frequency-domain bases to guide the model with the overall distribution of the input, thereby substantially reducing the number of parameters updated during the online phase. Specifically, CoSPOT decomposes time series into frequency bases and composes the corresponding spectral basis prompts according to their amplitudes, allowing unseen patterns to be represented as new combinations of learned basis prompts. Our extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority and practicality of CoSPOT across challenging online scenarios, including extended online phases and cross-dataset settings with substantial distribution shifts. Our code is available at https://github.com/seungyoon-Choi/CoSPOT.

title: Geometric Information Theory for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the integration of geometric information theory (GIT) into quantum computation, aiming to enhance both the efficiency and reliability of quantum algorithms. GIT, a framework that quantifies the information content of geometric structures, offers a novel approach to optimizing quantum operations. We detail the application of GIT to key quantum computing processes, including quantum gate design, error correction, and measurement. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging geometric properties to improve the overall performance of quantum systems. The paper presents a preliminary investigation into how GIT can contribute to reduced computational complexity and enhanced robustness within quantum computation.

title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Kernel Selection (BGCA-AKS)
abstract: Standard Bayesian Geometric Chaos theory relies on a fixed kernel function, often failing to adequately capture the inherent variability within complex systems. Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Kernel Selection (BGCA-AKS) addresses this limitation by implementing an adaptive kernel selection mechanism. This method dynamically adjusts the kernel based on observational data, resulting in more robust and predictive chaos models. The core mechanism involves an iterative Bayesian update scheme that incorporates observational data to refine the kernel weights, creating a dynamically adaptive representation of the system's uncertainty. This approach significantly enhances the model's capacity to represent and predict chaotic behavior.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Dynamic Adjustment Mechanism
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive neural network training mechanism that utilizes dynamic weight adjustment to enhance model generalization and adaptability. Traditional neural network training often relies on fixed parameters, which struggles to adapt to data distribution shifts. Our proposed method employs a learning algorithm to continuously optimize network parameters, leading to improved performance. The core focus is on dynamically adjusting the network's weights, offering a novel approach to address this challenge.

title: Non-Linear Constraint Optimization for Biological Systems
abstract: This research investigates the application of non-linear constraint optimization to biological systems, specifically focusing on optimization of gene expression and protein folding. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and dynamic nature of biological systems, necessitating novel approaches that can effectively capture evolutionary principles and adapt to changing conditions. This paper proposes a hybrid method integrating evolutionary algorithms with constraint optimization, incorporating feedback from the system's own adaptive behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in optimizing a simplified biological model, highlighting its potential for broader applicability in the analysis and control of complex biological processes.

title: Quantum Entanglement Self-Organizing Structure Modeling and Control
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for transformative technologies. This paper explores the potential of leveraging entanglement to model and control quantum systems, specifically focusing on the development of a novel self-organizing structure model. We propose a method that utilizes the inherent properties of entanglement to guide the formation and manipulation of quantum states, leading to enhanced control and precision. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum system exhibiting self-organization through carefully orchestrated entanglement adjustments. This research introduces a new quantum control algorithm predicated on this self-organization principle. The primary motivation is to address the current limitations in harnessing entanglement for practical applications, particularly concerning the development of robust and controllable quantum systems.

title: 基于物理约束的程序合成
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis based on physical constraints. The core idea is to leverage physical constraint theory to automatically generate programs that satisfy specified constraints. Traditional program synthesis methods often rely on abstract specifications, leading to solutions that may not perfectly align with the underlying physical reality of a system. This work introduces a mechanism where system constraints are mathematically modeled, and then program synthesis techniques are applied to generate code that precisely adheres to these constraints. The approach offers a more direct and potentially more accurate method for program generation, particularly in domains where physical laws and constraints are dominant. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through a theoretical framework, without requiring empirical experimentation. The core equation driving this approach is: `P = F(C)`, where `P` represents the generated program, `F` denotes the program synthesis function, and `C` represents the set of physical constraints. Furthermore, the key operational formula is `C → P`, signifying the constraint-to-program transformation. This framework aims to bridge the gap between formal specification and executable code by directly incorporating physical constraints into the synthesis process.

title: Deep Learning and Symbolic Logic Hybrid Reasoning Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for hybrid reasoning, integrating the strengths of deep learning and symbolic logic. The core idea is to combine the representation learning capabilities of deep neural networks with the logical inference capabilities of symbolic reasoning systems. We introduce a framework that utilizes a deep learning model to generate representations and a symbolic logic engine to perform logical inference on these representations, leveraging a knowledge graph as a bridge for seamless knowledge transfer and fusion. The framework addresses the limitations of each approach individually – deep learning's struggle with explicit knowledge representation and symbolic logic's difficulty in handling complex, high-dimensional data – and ultimately aims to create more robust and intelligent systems capable of both learning from data and reasoning logically. This work provides a foundational approach for building systems that can effectively combine the benefits of both worlds, leading to improved knowledge representation, reasoning accuracy, and overall intelligent behavior. ---

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Infrastructure Management
abstract: This research investigates the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to the autonomous management of complex infrastructure systems. The core premise is that efficient infrastructure operation necessitates coordinated decision-making across numerous interconnected systems, such as energy grids and traffic networks. This paper proposes a framework where a team of agents, each trained via MARL, learns to optimize their respective tasks, ultimately contributing to the overall system performance. The agents interact within a simulated environment, receiving rewards based on their actions and the resultant impact on the system. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to provide a scalable and adaptable solution for infrastructure management challenges, moving beyond traditional centralized control methods. The key innovations lie in the decentralized learning approach and the application of MARL to a complex, dynamic real-world domain. The simulation environment incorporates realistic constraints and dynamic factors, allowing for robust agent training and evaluation. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key components and challenges of this MARL-based approach, and discuss potential future research directions. The overall goal is to develop a system capable of intelligently adapting to changing conditions and optimizing infrastructure operation in a manner that is both efficient and resilient.

title: Graph Representation Learning with Attention Mechanisms for Relational Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to graph representation learning that leverages attention mechanisms to enhance relational reasoning. Traditional graph embedding methods often treat all nodes and edges equally, failing to capture the complex relationships within a graph effectively. Our approach introduces an attention-based mechanism that dynamically assigns weights to nodes and edges, allowing the model to prioritize the most relevant connections when constructing node embeddings. This mechanism allows the model to focus on crucial information, leading to more expressive and informative representations of graph structures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and a detailed description of the implementation. The core of our method lies in learning contextualized embeddings where the influence of neighboring nodes and edges are weighted based on their importance to a given node. The resulting embeddings are expected to perform better on downstream relational reasoning tasks. The method's ability to adaptively focus on critical connections represents a significant advancement in graph representation learning.

title: Adaptive Neuron Topology Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design, termed Adaptive Neuron Topology Learning (ANTL). The core premise of ANTL is that the connection topology of a neural network can be dynamically adjusted based on the input data, leading to improved feature extraction and pattern recognition efficiency. We introduce a mechanism leveraging reinforcement learning wherein neurons autonomously evaluate their activation states and network performance to guide the adjustment of their connection weights and, consequently, the overall network topology. Unlike traditional neural network training methods which primarily focus on weight optimization, ANTL addresses the largely unexplored area of topology optimization, enabling networks to evolve and adapt in a data-driven manner. This research demonstrates the potential for ANTL to create more efficient and specialized neural networks for a wide range of applications. The key mathematical framework utilizes the following notations: $x_i$, $w_{ij}$, $\alpha_{ij}$, $\delta_{ij}$, $R_{ij}$, $S_{ij}$, $\rho_{ij}$, $L_{ij}$, $\eta$, $\gamma$, $\theta_{ij}$, $Q$, $A$, $B$, $C$, $Z$, $N$, $K$, $U$, $V$, $f(x)$.

title: Symbolic Regression with Quantum Annealing for Discovering New Mathematical Equations
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum annealing to the field of symbolic regression, a technique for automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. The core idea is to frame the symbolic regression problem as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, which can then be solved using the quantum annealing algorithm. This approach aims to identify previously unknown mathematical relationships that accurately represent a given dataset. The paper details the methodology, including the mapping process, the QUBO formulation, and the utilization of the quantum annealing solver. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, the potential for quantum annealing to outperform classical methods in certain scenarios, particularly when dealing with complex datasets and high-dimensional search spaces. The resulting equations are presented as a set of symbolic expressions, enabling both quantitative analysis and further investigation. The ultimate goal is to provide a framework for automated equation discovery, potentially leading to advancements in various scientific and engineering domains.

title: Dungeons That Build Themselves: A Comparative Analysis Review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of PCG and roguelikes as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Augmenting the Intelligence of Large Language Model-Based Agents with Graphs: A Survey
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance, prompting the development of LLM-based agents to tackle complex, open-world tasks. Despite these advances, autonomous agents still face critical bottlenecks in environmental perception, multi-step reasoning, and long-term opera-tional consistency. Graphs provide a systematic solution to these challenges by explicitly modeling entities, relationships, and dependencies, thereby establishing a rigorous foundation for reasoning and interaction. While recent literature explores this integration, existing surveys primarily focus on operational workflows and architectures, lacking a systematic analysis of how graphs fundamentally elevate agent intelligence. To bridge this gap, this survey presents a comprehensive review of Graph-Augmented LLM-based Agents (GLAs). We systematically decompose agent architecture to distill five core capabilities required for advanced intelligence: perception, reasoning, memorization, generaliza-tion, and interaction. We explicitly address why graphs are uniquely suited to bolster these capabilities and how they are practically integrated, proposing a novel taxonomy that organizes existing studies along these five dimensions. Furthermore, we review representative real-world applications of GLAs across diverse domains and outline key challenges and promising directions for future research. A curated repository containing the literature reviewed in this survey, along with the latest advancements in this field, is maintained and regularly updated at https://github.com/sqs17/GLA.

title: Turn-Based Combat Arena: A New Framework for Multiagent Training and Game Balancing
abstract: This paper is the first in a series on Turn-Based Combat Arena, a configurable framework for turn-based strategy games designed to support the efficient training and evaluation of machine learning agents. The proposed framework enables flexible modification of game rules and parameters, allowing rapid experimentation across diverse scenarios. Its architecture is optimized for high-throughput simulation, supporting tens of thousands of games per second and enabling the storage and processing of billions of gameplay records on a single machine. The problem of balancing the game, and particularly the parameters of game units, is investigated in detail. We evaluate several optimization approaches and show that multiple methods converge to comparable solutions, suggesting robustness in identifying balanced game configurations. These results indicate that the framework can serve as a practical platform for both game design analysis and agent training.

title: A Recursive Module-Coupling Algorithm for Computing Low-Energy Eigenstates
abstract: Finding the eigenstates of a many-body Hamiltonian is a fundamental challenge in physics and computational science. Since the search space grows exponentially with system size, numerous classical and quantum algorithms have been developed to address this problem. A practical strategy is to identify a physics-informed low-dimensional subspace that effectively accommodates the low-lying eigenstates, thereby reducing the computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a recursive module-coupling algorithm, which iteratively treats a system as a composition of locally-coupled smaller modules, with low-energy subspace estimated successively according to the same recursive structure. Unlike the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) approach that optimizes a global matrix product state through repeated local sweeps and obtains excited states sequentially, our algorithm constructs a physically tailored variational basis from module eigenstates and obtains several low-energy states on an equal footing, leading to substantial speedups if targeting moderate accuracy. Our proposed method further leads naturally to a recursive quantum variational algorithm, providing a systematic and modular circuit-construction framework compatible with contemporary gate-based quantum architectures. At each recursive level, block encoders are trained to map logical basis states onto the retained physical subspace, within which a variational circuit is subsequently optimized. Such a quantum-circuit implementation provides not only a quantum multistate eigensolver, but also a systematic prescription for hierarchically constructing quantum state-preparation circuits. Classical simulations demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method, whereas experiments on IBM quantum processors show that eigenstate preparation with reasonable fidelities is achievable even in the current NISQ era.

title: Diffusion-Encoding Gaussian Field for Joint k-q dMRI Reconstruction
abstract: Diffusion MRI requires repeated k-space acquisitions over multiple diffusion-encoding directions, making acquisition time dependent on both spatial and angular sampling. Existing joint k-q methods either associate directional parameters with fixed voxels or separate spatial reconstruction from angular completion. However, diffusion-weighted images acquired under different directions share the same anatomical organization, while their local signal intensities vary with diffusion encoding. Existing formulations do not fully exploit the complementarity between shared anatomy and direction-dependent signal variation. Consequently, residual spatial errors may be misinterpreted as genuine angular variation and propagated to unobserved directions. We propose a subject-specific spatial-angular Gaussian field for self-supervised joint k-q dMRI reconstruction. Shared 3D Gaussian primitives provide local spatial support, with each primitive carrying a continuous q-conditioned tensor-residual response. The signal at each location is synthesized from multiple overlapping primitive responses, coupling neighboring spatial regions and diffusion directions. The field is progressively optimized from undersampled k-space measurements of observed directions, without fully sampled targets or held-out-direction supervision. Experiments on three HCP diffusion shells under multiple acceleration settings demonstrated consistent improvements in missing-direction DWI reconstruction, tensor-derived metrics, and principal diffusion orientation estimation.

title: Beyond Outcome Gaps: Process-Aware Fairness Diagnosis for LLM-based Multi-Agent Decision Systems
abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly considered for high-stakes decision-making, yet outcome-based fairness audits can miss where risks arise within the decision trajectory. We present SCOPED-Hiring, a process-aware fairness diagnosis pipeline for LLM-based hiring MAS. SCOPED-Hiring constructs controlled resume variants, runs role-based hiring committees, logs over 311K structured decision trajectories, and converts trajectory fields into quantitative fairness signals organized by six diagnostic lenses: final outcome, counterfactual, process, pathway, dynamic, and design effects. SCOPED-Hiring reveals that balanced final hire rates can mask hidden trajectory unfairness in multi-agent decision trajectories: career gaps trigger suspicion, proxy cues shape qualification judgments, and identity cues lead to unequal investigation. Targeted repair guided by these diagnoses reduces total layered burden by 72.3% while shifting the hire rate by only 1.86 pp, showing that process diagnosis can guide effective repair. SCOPED-Hiring constructs controlled resume variants, runs role-based hiring committees, logs over 311K structured decision trajectories, and converts trajectory fields into quantitative fairness signals organized by six diagnostic lenses: final outcome, counterfactual, process, pathway, dynamic, and design effects. SCOPED-Hiring reveals that balanced final hire rates can mask hidden trajectory unfairness in multi-agent decision trajectories: career gaps trigger suspicion, proxy cues shape qualification judgments, and identity cues lead to unequal investigation. Targeted repair guided by these diagnoses reduces total layered burden by 72.3% while shifting the hire rate by only 1.86 pp, showing that process diagnosis can guide effective repair. title: Title: Quantum Wavefunction Collapse as a Computational Resource Allocation Scheme
abstract: Quantum wavefunctions represent the fundamental building blocks of quantum systems, and their collapse into definite states is a crucial aspect of quantum computation. This paper explores a novel computational model centered around the concept of 'wavefunction collapse' as a dynamic resource allocation scheme. Traditional approaches often focus on the abrupt collapse of a single wavefunction, whereas we propose a system where wavefunction states are treated as 'resource units' that can be allocated and repurposed based on task-specific requirements. This shift aims to overcome the limitations of standard collapse models and potentially unlock new avenues for quantum computing. The core mechanism involves introducing a 'wavefunction state vector' representation, allowing for a more granular control over quantum state evolution through a probabilistic allocation algorithm. This research investigates the potential of this approach to enhance computational efficiency and explore novel applications within the quantum realm.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encryption Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, is increasingly recognized as a potential cornerstone for secure communication. This paper explores the design of a novel cryptographic algorithm based on quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve absolute security against potential attacks from quantum computers. The core principle revolves around establishing a quantum entangled state, representing a shared secret, and utilizing its properties within a novel encryption protocol employing quantum measurements for key decryption. This approach offers a promising solution to the challenges posed by quantum computing, providing a foundation for robust data security. We delve into the algorithm's design, the underlying quantum mechanics, and the potential for high tolerance to measurement errors.

The core mechanism involves leveraging entangled quantum states to rapidly compute probability distributions, thereby improving model accuracy compared to classical optimization techniques. The paper explores the potential of QAPMO to address limitations in traditional optimization methods and offers a promising path towards more efficient probabilistic model design.

abstract: Quantum-enhanced phase field, a paradigm shift in computational materials science, promises to revolutionize the design process by dramatically reducing the computational cost associated with simulating complex material properties. This paper explores the implementation of a novel quantum phase field, leveraging superposition and entanglement to accelerate the calculation of phase fields, offering a significant advancement over traditional methods. We detail the design of this quantum algorithm, emphasizing its potential to drastically reduce computational time and improve the efficiency of material discovery. The core mechanism centers around representing multiple phases simultaneously using quantum superposition, allowing for a more efficient exploration of the vast design space. The potential impact of this technology on materials research is substantial, offering a path towards faster innovation in areas like superconductivity, thermoelectricity, and light-emitting materials.

title: Title: Multi-Level Bayesian Inference – Automated Discovery of Underlying Structures
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian inference algorithm, Multi-Level Bayesian Inference (MLBI), designed to automatically discover complex structures within data beyond traditional statistical methods. The core mechanism revolves around the incorporation of a 'structured uncertainty' – a measure of inherent complexity and interconnectedness – within the model's framework. MLBI iteratively refines the model based on this uncertainty, facilitating a deeper understanding of the data's underlying structure. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis of the algorithm's convergence properties and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of illustrative examples. The paper emphasizes the potential for MLBI to uncover previously hidden patterns and relationships, offering a significant advancement in data analysis and structural discovery.

title: Temporal Graph Embeddings with Causality Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that explicitly incorporates temporal dynamics and causal relationships. Traditional graph embedding methods typically treat graphs as static structures, neglecting the evolution of nodes over time and the underlying causal dependencies. Our method leverages a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representation of the graph, enriched with timestamps and causal links. We employ a learned Markov chain model constrained by the DAG to predict future node states, generating embeddings that capture both temporal dependencies and causal reasoning. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of temporal modeling and causal inference within a graph embedding framework. The resulting embeddings are expected to outperform existing methods in tasks requiring understanding of temporal patterns and causal influences within the graph structure. The core algorithm is presented, and the theoretical foundations underlying the approach are discussed. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method through a detailed analysis of the embedding learning process and illustrate its potential with illustrative examples.

title: Multi-Dimensional Geometric Topology Verification for Quantum Computing Validation
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of multi-dimensional geometric topology as a novel validation method for quantum computing algorithms, specifically focusing on the rigorous verification of algorithm effectiveness within complex multi-dimensional spaces. Traditional quantum computing validation methods often struggle with intricate topological problems, necessitating a fundamentally new approach. We present a framework for applying topological properties to quantum algorithm verification, leveraging the inherent characteristics of quantum computation to address these challenges. This research aims to provide a robust and potentially transformative validation technique for quantum computing, ensuring the reliability and correctness of quantum algorithms across diverse environments. The core claim is that exploring this new validation methodology will significantly improve the validation process, allowing for the assurance of algorithm correctness and performance.

title: Title: Topology-Based Cryptography with Dynamic Key Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel cryptographic system leveraging topology for dynamic key generation. Traditional cryptographic keys are static, making them vulnerable to brute-force attacks. This research proposes a system that constructs keys through a self-replicating topological structure, ensuring inherent resistance against manipulation. The core mechanism involves a constantly evolving topology generated from user interaction data, making it computationally infeasible to reverse engineer the key. The system's robustness stems from the inherent difficulty of manipulating a topology without affecting the underlying data, thereby rendering key reconstruction impossible. We explore the design and implementation of this system, detailing its mathematical foundation and demonstrating its potential for enhanced security.

title: Explainable AI using Causal Mediation Analysis of Neural Networks
abstract: The increasing deployment of neural networks in critical applications necessitates robust methods for understanding their decision-making processes. Traditional explainable AI (XAI) techniques, such as feature attribution methods, often provide superficial explanations, failing to reveal the underlying causal mechanisms driving predictions. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging Causal Mediation Analysis (CMA) to provide truly explainable AI by analyzing neural networks. The core idea is to train a mediation model alongside the neural network, allowing us to quantify the pathways through which inputs mediate the network's output. This approach moves beyond simply identifying influential features to uncovering the causal relationships governing the network's behavior. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method, highlighting its potential to generate more insightful and trustworthy explanations for neural network predictions. The methodology includes defining causal pathways, constructing a mediation model, and interpreting the results to understand the mechanisms underlying network decisions. This work offers a significant advancement in XAI, providing a framework for building AI systems that are not just accurate but also understandable.

title: Neuro-Net Dynamic Topology Optimization (NDTOO)
abstract: This paper introduces Neuro-Net Dynamic Topology Optimization (NDTOO), a novel approach to neural network design that leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize the network's connection topology. Inspired by the self-organizing processes observed in biological neural networks, NDTO simulates an evolutionary system where the network's topology adapts over time to improve learning performance. The core mechanism involves a reinforcement learning agent, typically a policy gradient method, interacting with the network to evaluate the impact of different connection topologies on metrics such as error and convergence speed. Based on these evaluations, the agent adjusts both connection weights and topology (e.g., adding, removing, or reshaping connections) to minimize error and maximize generalization ability. A key element is the incorporation of a "topology mutation" mechanism, mimicking synaptic plasticity in biological neurons, which accelerates the optimization process. NDTO represents a significant departure from traditional neural network optimization techniques, which primarily focus on static weight adjustments or limited topology changes. By treating topology as a primary optimization variable, NDTO aims to achieve superior performance and robustness.

title: A novel use of AI for prediction of clinical deterioration in a post-acute hospital
abstract: There is a growing literature on the prediction of risk of deterioration in hospital settings, including by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) models. However, this literature has focused on acute-care hospitals, rather than post-acute facilities, where the risk of deterioration remains high. Post-acute facilities tend to have lower digital maturity and poorer data foundations, as well as less rich physiologic data, making the implementation of AI tools for deterioration challenging. In this study, we demonstrate a novel use of AI for the prediction of clinical deterioration in a post-acute hospital. Despite clinical and technical barriers, we developed a meaningful predictive model (sensitivity = 82%). Further, the patterns of contribution to risk of deterioration from the primary contributing variables were remarkably physiologic. This demonstrates a novel model for the prediction of deterioration in an understudied context and provides novel evidence for physiologic predictors of deterioration consistent with previous acute-care scoring systems in the post-acute environment.

title: Chemical and geometric representation fidelity improves drug--target affinity prediction
abstract: Predicting drug--target binding affinity (DTA) requires models to distinguish subtle chemical and structural determinants underlying molecular recognition. Although recent approaches increasingly incorporate richer drug and protein information, such information may be compressed, homogenized or discretized during representation construction, causing affinity-relevant distinctions to be lost before interaction modelling. We hypothesized that this representation-stage information loss constitutes an upstream bottleneck that cannot be reliably overcome by increasingly complex interaction predictors. To test this hypothesis, we developed ReGeoDTA, a representation-preserving framework that maintains affinity-relevant chemical heterogeneity in molecular representations and continuous geometric relationships in protein structures. Across three benchmark datasets, ReGeoDTA consistently improved affinity prediction, and the proposed representation-preserving strategies retained their benefits across diverse DTA architectures. Controlled representation degradation progressively reduced predictive performance, whereas increasing downstream predictor complexity failed to recover information lost during representation construction. These findings identify representation fidelity as an upstream design principle for accurate and generalizable drug--target affinity prediction, with potential implications for computational compound prioritization.

title: Learning CNN Filters via Generalized Stein's Method
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have undoubtedly revolutionized image data analysis and the field of computer vision. As the cornerstone of CNNs, the convolution operation enables the networks to extract abstract features and uncover hidden relationships in the image data. This paper considers the problem of estimating convolution filters from a statistical perspective using a classical tool --- Stein's formula. We first formulate CNNs into a general index model with matrix-valued input, where convolution filters can be viewed as index vectors. Furthermore, we propose a novel singular value decomposition (SVD) based approach to accurately learn the convolution filters based on a generalized version of the first-order Stein's formula. Theoretical analysis suggests that our estimation achieves an optimal convergence rate, comparable to that of generalized linear models where the link function is known. Extensive simulation studies and real data analyses demonstrate that our approach outperforms popular deep learning algorithms, such as Adam. Notably, our method extends beyond filter estimation and can be applied to nonlinear dimension reduction, providing a viable pathway for representation learning.

title: Broadband high-level squeezed light using waveguide optical parametric amplifiers with external dispersion compensation
abstract: We demonstrate broadband phase-sensitive amplification (PSA) measurement of squeezed light generated by a waveguide optical parametric amplifier (OPA) with external dispersion compensation. In broadband systems, group velocity dispersion (GVD) induces a frequency-dependent rotation of the squeezing axis, which limits the observable bandwidth in PSA measurements. While dispersion compensation between two OPAs has been demonstrated previously, we show that the quantity to be compensated is not the material group-delay dispersion D itself but a gain-dependent effective value D tanh ⁡ r /(2 r ), where r is the squeezing parameter, and realize the compensation with free-space fused-silica plates whose insertion loss is 0.4%. As a result, we observe a maximum squeezing of 5.9 ± 0.2 dB near the carrier frequency and more than 5 dB of squeezing up to a frequency offset of 5.9 ± 0.1 THz from the carrier. Furthermore, squeezing below the shot-noise level is confirmed up to a frequency offset of 6.9 ± 0.1 THz from the carrier, corresponding to the accessible phase-matching bandwidth of the waveguide OPA. Our results establish a practical method for broadband characterization of squeezed light and provide a key step toward ultrafast continuous-variable quantum information processing.

As a result, we observe a maximum squeezing of 5.9 ± 0.2 dB near the carrier frequency and more than 5 dB of squeezing up to a frequency offset of 5.9 ± 0.1 THz from the carrier. Furthermore, squeezing below the shot-noise level is confirmed up to a frequency offset of 6.9 ± 0.1 THz from the carrier, corresponding to the accessible phase-matching bandwidth of the waveguide OPA. Our results establish a practical method for broadband characterization of squeezed light and provide a key step toward ultrafast continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Estudo Inicial do Problema do Caixeiro Viajante utilizando Computação Quântica
abstract: Este artigo apresenta um estudo inicial sobre o uso de computação quântica para o Problema do Caixeiro Viajante (TSP), explorando sua modelagem por grafos e sua relação com formulações QUBO, QAOA e Quantum Annealing. A partir de uma implementação preliminar em Qiskit, o trabalho organiza abordagens relacionadas e define critérios para comparar algoritmos clássicos, híbridos e quânticos em instâncias controladas, considerando desempenho, qualidade das rotas e limitações de dispositivos NISQ.

title: Nonlinear Random Matrix Self-Adaptive Learning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive learning framework based on non-linear random matrices. Traditional machine learning models often rely on predefined objectives, limiting their ability to effectively handle complex data distributions. This framework dynamically adjusts matrix parameters based on data distribution shifts, enabling automated learning of more efficient functions. The core mechanism utilizes a "adaptive weight" update process, incorporating the random matrix's dynamics with the principles of deep learning's self-adaptation. The proposed approach demonstrates superior generalization performance across diverse data distributions.

title: Quantum Information Cryptography Geometric Optimization
abstract: Quantum Information Cryptography (QIC) is a field focused on developing secure communication methods leveraging quantum mechanics. A crucial aspect of QIC is the design of cryptographic algorithms that are resilient to attacks, particularly those exploiting weaknesses in mathematical hardness. This paper explores the application of geometric optimization techniques to enhance the security of quantum information cryptography. We propose a novel framework that systematically optimizes key parameters within a quantum information cipher, aiming to mitigate potential vulnerabilities inherent in traditional cryptographic approaches. The core mechanism centers on utilizing geometric optimization to refine the fundamental structure of the cipher, thereby bolstering its resistance to attack. The potential benefits of this approach include enhanced key distribution, improved resistance to brute-force attacks, and increased robustness against known algorithmic weaknesses. This research presents a preliminary investigation into the efficacy of geometric optimization within QIC, demonstrating the potential for significant improvements in security.

title: Multi-Modal Coherence-Based Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding that transcends the limitations of single-mode quantum states. It leverages the inherent coherence within multi-mode quantum systems for robust and high-fidelity information storage and transmission. The core idea centers around precisely controlling the coherence time and phase relationships between multiple modes, enabling significantly higher information density compared to conventional methods. We introduce a new framework for quantum state design and encoding, specifically tailored to exploit multi-modal coherence. The theoretical framework presented here demonstrates the potential for achieving unprecedented levels of information storage and transmission by harnessing the complex correlations present in multi-modal quantum systems. The key advancements lie in recognizing and utilizing the intrinsic coherence present in multi-mode systems, leading to a fundamental shift in how quantum information is encoded. This work lays the groundwork for future research into advanced quantum information processing technologies.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Error Correction and Decoding Protocol
abstract: This paper presents a novel protocol for quantum error correction and decoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core concept involves utilizing multi-particle entanglement to construct an iterative error-correcting code. This code operates through iterative correction cycles combined with quantum measurements, achieving high-fidelity information encoding and decoding despite the detrimental effects of quantum decoherence and noise. The primary innovation lies in the strategic exploitation of multi-body entanglement, a relatively underexplored area in existing quantum error correction schemes. The protocol's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the reliability of quantum communication and computation. The design incorporates key elements such as parity-check matrices tailored to the entangled state and optimized measurement strategies to minimize information loss during the decoding process. The presented approach represents a significant step towards building practical and robust quantum systems capable of handling the inherent challenges of quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Topological Structures of Unitary Matrices
abstract: Quantum topological matrices represent a fascinating intersection of quantum mechanics and topology, offering potential advantages in secure communication and quantum computing. This paper investigates the topological properties of unitary matrices through the application of topology analysis. We explore the relationship between the mathematical structure of unitary matrices and the underlying physical phenomena, demonstrating how topology provides a powerful tool for analyzing and understanding their behavior. The core claim is that the study of quantum topological matrices reveals crucial insights into their potential for physical applications, particularly in the realm of secure cryptography. The paper details a methodology for analyzing the topological aspects of unitary matrices, ultimately leading to a novel understanding of their potential.

title: Nonlinear Time Series Complexity Assessment
abstract: This paper investigates the complexity assessment of time series data, specifically focusing on identifying anomalous patterns within complex datasets. The core of this work centers around a novel algorithm predicated on the analysis of non-linear time series, designed to pinpoint subtle deviations indicative of complex behavior. The proposed method leverages the inherent unpredictability of these sequences to create a robust and accurate metric for anomaly detection. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, the underlying mathematical principles, and its application to a variety of time series datasets. The primary goal is to provide a more precise and insightful approach to analyzing time series data, minimizing the risk of false positives and maximizing the detection of genuine anomalies. The research explores the potential benefits of this approach in various fields, including financial forecasting, industrial process monitoring, and biological signal analysis.

title: Topological Quantum States for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper presents a novel architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing leveraging the unique properties of topological quantum states. The core idea revolves around harnessing the inherent robustness of these states against local perturbations, thereby mitigating the detrimental effects of quantum decoherence and enabling high-fidelity quantum computation. The proposed architecture utilizes non-local entanglement generated from topological quantum states to facilitate quantum information transmission and storage. Furthermore, a fault-tolerant circuit is constructed, incorporating redundancy encoding and error detection mechanisms to ensure reliable quantum computations. The paper details the theoretical framework and key components of this architecture, highlighting its potential to overcome the limitations of traditional quantum computing approaches and represent a significant step toward practical, scalable quantum computation. The focus is on the design principles and the underlying mathematical foundations that support this architecture.

title: Distributed Quantum Error Correction via Information Entropy Topology
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed quantum error correction (QEC) leveraging the concept of information entropy topology. Traditional QEC focuses on coding schemes and error detection/correction algorithms, often treating the underlying network topology as a secondary consideration. We argue that the topology itself can be fundamentally defined and optimized using information entropy, offering a new paradigm for constructing more robust and efficient QEC networks. We present a framework where quantum error correction nodes are viewed as points within an information entropy space, and their connectivity is determined by the geodesic distance – a measure derived from information entropy – between them. This approach allows for the direct optimization of the network topology to achieve superior error correction performance. The core claim is that utilizing information entropy to define and operate on quantum error correction networks significantly enhances their error resilience and correction capabilities. The key mechanism involves translating quantum error correction networks into a topological structure within an information entropy space, exploiting the geometric properties of information entropy to refine the design of error-correcting codes and optimize the error detection/correction processes. Specifically, we employ information entropy distances to define the relationships between correction nodes, creating networks with tailored error correction properties. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis, that this entropy-based topology can outperform conventional approaches, particularly in scenarios with complex network geometries and high error rates. The research contributes to a deeper understanding of the interplay between information theory and quantum error correction, paving the way for the development of next-generation QEC systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Multi-Variable Probability Distribution Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to probabilistic model prediction, focusing on adaptive multi-variable distributions. We introduce a dynamic model that automatically adjusts probability distributions based on observed data, leveraging deep learning for parameter learning and optimization. The core mechanism involves a learned probability adaptation process, enabling more precise model predictions than traditional approaches. This work addresses the limitations of static parameterization in probabilistic modeling and offers a dynamically responsive system for improved predictive accuracy.

title: Adaptive Meta-Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to meta-learning termed Adaptive Meta-Learning, which addresses the challenges of slow convergence and limited generalization often encountered in traditional meta-learning paradigms. The core idea is to dynamically adjust both the difficulty of individual learning tasks and the meta-learning strategy itself, creating a truly adaptive learning process. This is achieved through a mechanism that continuously monitors task performance and task relationships, enabling real-time modification of parameters such as learning rates, network architectures, and data sampling strategies. We demonstrate that this adaptive approach significantly improves learning speed and generalization capabilities compared to fixed-strategy meta-learning. The key innovation lies in the introduction of task-specific adaptation, which enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of the meta-learning process. The presented framework offers a promising direction for developing more robust and scalable meta-learning systems.
